messages:
acme-admin: hey - we accepted the external collaborator invite this morning but when our user tries to open the project console they get a 403. worked yesterday, nothing changed on our side. any ideas? :confused:

maria (Support): sorry about that. can you paste the exact error or a screenshot? is the user internal (same org) or external guest?

acme-admin: external guest from another Okta tenant. this is what the browser shows: 

`403 — You do not have permission to view this project`

and when they try the api it returns: 
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer user-token" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/pm-abc123/members
# HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
# {"error":"permission_denied","message":"caller lacks permission: view_project"}
```

maria (Support): thanks. can you confirm the account email (masked ok) and the project id? also was this invite via the invite link (external) or via SCIM group mapping?

acme-admin: email is j.smith@partnerco.com, project id pm-abc123, invite was via the external invite link we sent last week (not SCIM).

raj (IAM): quick checklist: 1) external collaborators are modeled as "external_user" principals; 2) org-level collaborator adds membership at org scope but not necessarily project scope unless the invite included project binding; 3) invites created from the org invite link have a flag to grant project bindings. my hunch: invite was created without the project-binding checkbox.

sam (SRE): I pulled authz logs for principal j.smith@partnerco.com. saw repeated denies: 

```
timestamp=2028-03-15T09:12:07Z component=authz decision=DENY principal_type=external_user principal_id=ext-u-98765 resource=project/pm-abc123 action=view_project reason=missing_project_binding
```

sam (SRE): so the platform recognizes the external principal but there's no project-level role attached. that matches raj's theory.

maria (Support): ok, options: 1) manually add j.smith@partnerco.com as a project member with the required role (fastest); 2) re-issue the invite with project-binding enabled; 3) if you expect many external users via invites, use SCIM group provisioning or invite templates that include project bindings. which would you prefer?

acme-admin: manual add works for now. how do we do that from the console?

maria (Support): Console -> Project pm-abc123 -> Settings -> Access -> Invite member -> enter email -> pick role -> send. for automation/cli you can use the API: 
```
POST /v1/projects/pm-abc123/members
Authorization: Bearer <org-admin-token>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "email": "j.smith@partnerco.com",
  "role": "viewer",
  "membership_type": "external_collaborator"
}
```

maria (Support): one caveat: if you later revoke and re-invite via the old invite link without the binding flag, the same issue will happen. recommend creating a new invite template that includes the project binding.

acme-admin: manual add worked, user can see the project now, thanks! is there anything you all will change on your side to prevent this?

raj (IAM): filing an engineering issue. observed pattern: invite-link creation UI doesn't surface the project-binding flag when an org admin creates an invite from the org settings -> invites flow. repro steps and a minimal failing unit test attached. assigning to eng-iam and tagging RED-1234. :memo:

sam (SRE): added a shortterm alert in the authz monitor to detect external principals hitting repeated missing_project_binding denies; will notify support if spike.

maria (Support): documenting workaround in KB: "External collaborator accepted invite but cannot access project (403)" with steps: verify invite type, manually apply project membership, re-issue invite with binding, consider SCIM for scale. linking to this thread. :link:

invite-bot: invite accepted event: external-invite ext-inv-5543 by acme-admin at 2028-03-15T08:45:12Z

acme-admin: thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround. closing the ticket once we verify no other users impacted. :thumbsup:
